edit.description: the operator logger's sink, whose `info` is the engine default's stdout write
whatever reads a narration line off a verb's stdout today

summary: every level of the CLI's stamped narration writes to stderr, so a verb's stdout carries only what the verb itself produced

per.section: A log line carries the instant it was written

acceptance: an `info` line through the CLI's operator logger reaches stderr and not stdout, `warn` and `error` land where they already did, and a verb's own listing still reaches stdout
tests: the CLI's stamped narration writes an info line to stderr
a verb's own listing reaches stdout while the narration of the same run does not
pins: the engine's consoleLogger still writes an info line to stdout
notes: `operatorLog` takes `consoleLogger` as its sink, whose `info` is `console.log`, so supervisor and tick-child narration lands on stdout today — which `docs/CLI.md`, *Narration carries the instant it was written* already states it does not. The engine default stays what it is: the same section leaves an embedder's `Logger` its own timing and its own streams.
